quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: In ideal conditions, use a four-second following distance. Increase this distance at night and in bad weather when it is harder to see.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt before starting the car. Check that all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If a car has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together. Always wear your seat belt, even if the car has airbags.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it harder for you to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it harder for you to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can reduce your ability to drive safely. If you are worried, angry, sad, or upset, your concentration suffers. Wait to drive until you feel calm.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not back up, stop, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How can you remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers do not speed this up.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when you change lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting adequate rest and staying alert.
Paying attention and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions causes many accidents. Always drive at a safe speed and with traffic flow.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood to show other drivers your car is disabled.

questions.question: You must report a crash to police when:
questions.explanation: Report a crash if anyone is injured or if damage is $1,000 or more.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces your alertness and concentration, slows your reaction time, and hurts your coordination.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. Never drink and drive. It is not safe.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus turns.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning, then turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning, then turn.
questions.explanation: Do not squeeze your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn before you turn.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You will see this sign at intersections where U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign with a traffic signal tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning left.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, turn on your emergency flashers and get off the road if you can. This helps other drivers see you and stay safe.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of a large truck or bus?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of one, the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, you should:
questions.explanation: In a crash, stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if anyone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What can impair a person's ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns you that wet pavement may be slippery and hard to control.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both can be stronger.
The effects of both can be weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects are weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both can be stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can increase the effects of both. For example, one drink taken with a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill road.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.

questions.question: When you see an angry driver, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Do not make eye contact or hand gestures. Slow down or move over to avoid them and stay safe.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and focus on driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a yield sign is coming. Begin to slow down when you see it.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or pulling into traffic. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after taking either one, and even more dangerous after combining them.

questions.question: You cannot pass another car:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing ahead, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not drive around the gate.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. This is:

options.text: Only needed when other cars are nearby.
A good habit and required by law.
Only needed during the move, not before.
Not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid on sharp turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: If a pedestrian crosses in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must stop for them.

questions.question: When you see a steady green light, you should:

options.text: Keep driving unless cars or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless cars or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and cars already in the intersection. You can keep driving, but go at a speed where you can stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may come from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, so does the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because impatient drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: As blood alcohol content (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer than those from your right. Check across the whole intersection before moving to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: While driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop in these situations: at a stop sign, at a red light, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: To help others see you as daylight fades, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades. Use high beams only when driving in an empty area with no other drivers.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe and protect other drivers.

questions.question: When changing lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What happens if you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effects.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The mixture can greatly increase the effects of both.
They have no effect on each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mixture can greatly increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and medicine together increase their harmful effects. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, give the right of way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Complete your turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use arm signals to show other drivers what they plan to do. A straight left arm means a left turn.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour on a long trip. If possible, share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. Let any traffic or pedestrians in the intersection pass first, then proceed when it is safe.
